$comment: Locates the upstream Docusaurus docs repo (OffchainLabs/arbitrum-docs) and pins the comparison
window, so a multi-day sync is not chasing a moving target while upstream keeps committing.
Resolution order, implemented in scripts/lib/upstream-tree.mjs: the --tree-a flag (which names
the docs tree itself), then the UPSTREAM_DOCS_REPO env var, then `repo` below, then `probePaths`.
The flag and the env var resolve against the cwd; `repo` and `probePaths` resolve against this
repo's root, so they keep working from a git worktree, where the cwd sits one level deeper.
Every source except --tree-a names the repo root, so `docsSubdir` is appended to it. When nothing
resolves, upstream-drift prints the full search order and exits 1.
This file is checked in on purpose: .gitignore excludes .env*, so an env-file default could not be
shared, which is why a machine-specific absolute path was hardcoded in upstream-drift.mjs before.
absentAllowlistComment: Upstream pages that are deliberately not ported, so reporting them as ABSENT is a false positive
that teaches readers to skim the drift report. A page belongs here only when its content is
accounted for somewhere else; a page that is merely low priority does not.
Every entry carries the reason it is exempt, and drift prints the count it suppressed.
Every entry records reviewedUpstreamSha: the git blob hash of the upstream file when a human read
it and granted the exemption. Drift recomputes that hash on each run and re-flags the pair as
STALE-ALLOWLIST once upstream edits the page, because an exemption is a judgement about one
version of a page, not a permanent one. Without it, allowlisting a page is the surest way to hide
a real gap that lands in it later. Re-read both pages, then update the hash (git hash-object
docs/<path> in the upstream checkout) or drop the entry.

absentAllowlist.reason: Content maps were replaced by index.mdx plus meta.json by design. Upstream's Docusaurus <Card> grid has no counterpart here because Fumadocs builds the same navigation from meta.json.

guttedAllowlistComment: Upstream pages that ARE ported at content parity but still trip the 70% body-line ratio, because
the count includes lines the port does not carry: Docusaurus `import` statements and inline
grid-style boilerplate. Reporting these as GUTTED is a false positive.
Separate from absentAllowlist on purpose. Absent-exempt means the page was never ported;
gutted-exempt means it was ported in full and only the line count disagrees. A single list would
let an exemption earned for one reason quietly cover the other.
Add an entry only after reading both pages side by side and confirming the content matches.
Every entry records reviewedUpstreamSha: the git blob hash of the upstream file when a human read
it and granted the exemption. Drift recomputes that hash on each run and re-flags the pair as
STALE-ALLOWLIST once upstream edits the page, because an exemption is a judgement about one
version of a page, not a permanent one. Without it, allowlisting a page is the surest way to hide
a real gap that lands in it later. Re-read both pages, then update the hash (git hash-object
docs/<path> in the upstream checkout) or drop the entry.

guttedAllowlist.reason: Confirmed at full parity with upstream by the FS-2655 side-by-side review. The 0.61 ratio is Docusaurus import boilerplate the port does not carry.
A deliberate card-landing rewrite, not a trim: the get-started landing was replaced by index.mdx plus cards by design. The remaining line gap is import lines and inline grid styling.
The same deliberate card-landing rewrite as get-started, confirmed by the FS-2655 side-by-side review. Upstream's content-map format has no counterpart here.

A deliberate restructure, not a trim: the local page folds upstream's per-feature bullet blocks into comparison tables. A sentence-level comparison by the FS-2652 agent found every upstream block present, so the 0.51 ratio measures format, not content.
